notes: Group F audit (mixed-type, naive-doodle, neo-brutal-pop, old-web, paddock-pass). Line ranges are from js/aesthetics/<key>.js and css/aesthetics/<key>.css as read on 2026-11-06; css ranges for large kit blocks point at the block's signature comment plus the key rules. Schema gaps: (1) `appSafe` is one boolean per move, but several moves are app-safe as a CSS recipe and board-only as SVG art (tick-ruler, catalogue-number); they were split or set conservatively. (2) The schema has no field for headline-hook moves (def.headline): mixed-face-headline, per-word-tilt-headline and wordart-headline are marked needs-code because they emit markup through the headline hook, although a generic per-word styling hook in the framework could turn them into recipes. (3) `moveCoverage` is a single number; for naive-doodle the wobble generator is a real svg-generator move but the scene art that uses it is hand-placed. Cross-style merges worth checking in M1: highlight-word (5 styles, 5 variants), kicker-treatment (5), stepped-spinner (5), focus-ring-style (5), contrast-floor-adjust (4: a colour search loop each, different targets), leading-edge-bar (mixed-type primary rule vs paddock hi-vis strip), perforated-rule (NBP dashes vs paddock stub with end ticks), repeating-stripe-fill (naive hatch 45deg, NBP progress -45deg, old-web 90deg blocks).

styles.name: Mixed Type
styles.coreTrick: The headline is set word by word in four faces (brand heading, serif italic, heavy grotesk, mono), each scaled by capHeight(brand)/capHeight(voice) so capitals share one line, and the same four voices are shown as 'Aa' cells with cap/x-height/baseline guides.
styles.colourRecipe: Primary is only the CTA and selected-segment rule and never touches the type; canvas becomes paper (a 4.5% ink mix) with ink hairlines; the accent is the single coloured word (last headline word, serif italic, shaded to read as text via accent-ink) and a footer dot. A muted client colour just means less of that one spark; nothing depends on chroma.

remainder.what: Word-to-voice assignment (function words to mono, content words alternate heavy/brand, last word italic) and cap-height normalisation (size factor k per voice)
remainder.whyCode: Needs font metrics (table, canvas measureText fallback) and a stop-word heuristic; no CSS or token can compute k = capB/capVoice per brand face.

remainder.what: Voice resolution per brand: pick contrast faces that never repeat the brand family, with weight fallback chains
remainder.whyCode: Font-pairing search over the FONTS list with weight availability checks.

remainder.what: Specimen art: four 'Aa' cells whose guide lines are positioned from each voice's measured cap/x height, plus glyph rows and a size scale
remainder.whyCode: Guide y positions come from per-face metrics; cell geometry is computed, not styled.

remainder.what: Mono headline word hack: -0.13em tracking, ligatures off, margin to restore the word space; line-height 0 inline words
remainder.whyCode: Hand-tuned optical corrections that depend on the specific mono face at display size.

remainder.what: Built-screen voice mixing: stat labels get a serif-italic asterisk, lead stat in heavy grotesk at 2x, list names heavy caps, screen titles with a '(Fig. 2)' caption
remainder.whyCode: Per-component targeting of specific screen elements with voice-specific font maths (cap-height k factor); only partly generalisable.

styles.notes: The look is half kit (square, ink hairlines, hard 4px slug, ink inversion, bracketed fields; all recipes) and half type engine (mixed-face-headline and the specimen, which are code because they depend on measured font metrics). A framework without a metrics-aware headline hook would lose the signature.

styles.name: Naive Doodle
styles.coreTrick: Every outline is a seeded wobble path (a polyline resampled every few units and pushed along its normal by two summed low-frequency sines, loops overshooting their start) emitted as SVG data URIs per brand, with the colour as a hatched crayon fill offset a few pixels outside its outline.
styles.colourRecipe: Client primary/secondary/accent become crayons: same hue and chroma, lightness lifted until fixed warm-black pencil text reads 4.6:1 on them; paper is fixed cream #FFFBF2 with a graph grid (dark: client dark pressed to a deep warm slate, chalk ink). A muted client colour is lifted lighter and hatched, so it still works; a very dark one gets lifted to a pastel.

remainder.what: The hero drawing: smiley sun, 12 dash rays, scalloped clouds, hill coloured outside its line, three loop flowers, note with loop arrow
remainder.whyCode: Hand-placed coordinates for one specific scene; only the wobble/arc primitives are reusable, the composition is bespoke illustration.

remainder.what: ndKit specific shapes: toggle faces on/off, flag, star with offset fill, tab ellipse, ring, tick, cross, checkbox with overshooting sides
remainder.whyCode: Each is a hand-authored shape built from the wobble primitives; a framework would need a shape library or per-component glyph definitions.

remainder.what: Per-component alignment of drawn data-URI backgrounds to each control (stretched outline sizing, per-button walls between segments, outline bleed offsets)
remainder.whyCode: Dozens of pixel offsets so an SVG outline sits just outside each component without crossing labels; component-specific tuning.

remainder.what: Muted-text contrast loop and crayon lift
remainder.whyCode: Iterative colour search against fixed pencil/ink; tokens cannot express it.

styles.notes: The wobble generator is genuinely reusable (it is a parameterised svg-generator: amplitude, step, seed, overshoot) and carries the style across every kit component. What is lost without code is the hero scene and the tuned outline alignments. Dark mode swaps ink to chalk and paper to slate but keeps the same recipe.

styles.name: Neo-Brutal Pop
styles.coreTrick: Everything is a flat colour block with a 2-3px ink outline and a plain-ink hard offset shadow that lifts on hover and collapses on press, on a near-white paper canvas, with whole sections as 100% primary/accent colour fields and UI-object stickers (price tag, starburst, flower, checkbox, cursor) as art.
styles.colourRecipe: Primary is the CTA, selected fills and the type section field; secondary is chips, checkbox sticker and progress stripes; accent is the highlight sticker and the In use field; all used flat at 100% with on-colour text. Canvas becomes paper by mixing the client canvas 85-90% toward white (dark: ink mixed into canvas); shadows are ink in light mode and black in dark. A muted client palette yields flat pastel blocks that still read because of the ink outline; chip fill is searched down until ink text holds 7:1.

remainder.what: Sticker cluster composition: price tag, starburst (20-point), checkbox, flower, cursor, squiggle, each rotated and shadowed, placed at fixed coordinates
remainder.whyCode: Fixed hand-placed SVG layout; the star/flower/tag primitives are generatable but their arrangement is bespoke.

remainder.what: Deck Material sticker sheet and In-product page (Gumroad-style cover, price, buy button)
remainder.whyCode: Bespoke deck markup per style (def.deck hooks).

remainder.what: Flower stuck on the highlight word's edge, centred off the pill with computed offsets
remainder.whyCode: Pseudo-element placement tuned to the highlight block; a recipe could cover it but it is tied to the sticker art.

remainder.what: Chip-fill contrast search and muted-on-paper search
remainder.whyCode: Iterative colour loops against 7:1 and 4.5:1 targets.

styles.notes: The most recipe-like of the five: the whole kit is outline + hard shadow + flat fill + squish, with a few tunable numbers (border width 2 vs 3px, radii 6/10 vs 12/18, shadow offset 4-6px). Only the sticker art and deck pages are bespoke.

styles.name: Old Web
styles.coreTrick: Grey #C0C0C0 windows and buttons drawn with the exact four-tone Win9x bevel (white/#DFDFDF top-left, #808080/#0A0A0A bottom-right, swapped for sunken) with navy-to-primary title bars on a starfield tile, and a WordArt headline built from a stacked-text-shadow extrusion plus two clipped overlay copies forming a three-band gradient.
styles.colourRecipe: Primary only feeds the WordArt bands and the end of every title-bar gradient (navy #000080 into primary, falling back to #1084D0 when white cannot read at 3:1); secondary tints icons and one 88x31 badge; accent is NEW! badges, counter LEDs and the highlighted WordArt word. Window chrome, links and bevel greys are fixed. WordArt bands are searched to hold 3:1 on the page; a pale yellow primary on white switches to a saturated sunset ramp instead of going olive. A muted client colour mostly vanishes into a navy title bar.

remainder.what: WordArt band colours: light/mid/deep bands each holding 3:1 on the page, a yellow-on-white sunset ramp special case, and a dark extrusion colour
remainder.whyCode: Colour searches with hue-specific special cases; cannot be a token or fixed mix.

remainder.what: WordArt markup: each word is a base copy plus two clipped overlay copies at 36%/66% height so html2canvas keeps it
remainder.whyCode: Headline hook emitting three nested spans per word.

remainder.what: Homepage window art: menu bar, nav list with drawn icons, under-construction sign, marquee, visitor counter with LED digits, webring, What's New list, 88x31 badges, status bar
remainder.whyCode: Bespoke Web 1.0 furniture markup and copy; each piece is its own hand-built component.

remainder.what: Table panel with list-view column headers, folder icons, NEW! badge, segmented progress
remainder.whyCode: Custom panel hook (def.panels.list) with bespoke markup.

remainder.what: Win98 tab geometry (chosen tab taller and bold, others lower) and caption-button gradient stack
remainder.whyCode: Pixel-exact stacked gradients and per-state offsets; recipe-able only as a fixed Win98 component pack.

styles.notes: Bevel, title bar, starfield, link colours and dotted focus are recipes and carry the kit and board windows well. The WordArt headline and the homepage art are the bespoke part. Mostly ignores the client palette by design, so palette-agnostic only in the sense of using fixed colours.

styles.name: Paddock Pass
styles.coreTrick: A race-day credential: a hi-vis strip down the leading edge (full height on the board, 4px on every card and selected row), square corners and hairline-ruled spec rows (micro-caps label left, mono value right), with a race numeral, barcode and dot-matrix generated deterministically from the brand name.
styles.colourRecipe: Hi-vis is the brightest of the client's three colours that is saturated enough (luminance >= 8:1 vs black proxy, saturation >= 35), pushed to s>=88 and l 48-66, else neon #e4ff2e, used only as a fill with an on-colour label. Primary stays the brand colour and moves by the least lightness needed to hold 3:1 on ground and card and 4.6:1 for white or dark text (printPrimary). Ground is an ice blue-grey with 10% hue pull toward the brand (dark: navy). A muted palette falls back to the neon strip.

remainder.what: printPrimary: search lightness in both directions for the smallest move that satisfies 3:1 on two beds and 4.6:1 for text
remainder.whyCode: Bidirectional colour search with multiple constraints.

remainder.what: Hi-vis colour selection across three palette colours with neon fallback
remainder.whyCode: Selection by luminance/saturation threshold, not a mix.

remainder.what: Livery panel art composition: numeral box with chevrons, dot matrix, three spec rows, tick scale, clipped stripe bands, notches, stub with barcode and sector time
remainder.whyCode: Fixed hand-placed 520x340 SVG layout; individual primitives are generatable, the arrangement is not.

remainder.what: Deck Material specimens (boxed numeral card, perforated stub card, controls card)
remainder.whyCode: Bespoke deck markup.

remainder.what: Muted/edge/track contrast searches against three beds
remainder.whyCode: Iterative colour loops.

styles.notes: Kit is mostly recipes (square, hairline, strip, rocker key, chevron button); app screens carry no art per its own hard rule, so everything bespoke is board/deck. The colour logic (hi-vis pick, printPrimary) is the code-heavy part and is what makes the strip feel brand-derived.
